# Technical Speaker Enablement: Bridging the Gap from Insight to Impact

At Indeed, brilliant engineers and VPs were regularly taking the stage at global conferences like PyCon and Open Source Summit. However, support was fragmented; presenters had basic templates but lacked a formal framework for proposal writing, narrative structure, or delivery coaching.

Leveraging my background in **college-level Communication pedagogy**, I stepped in to transform "informal help" into a scalable, high-impact enablement program. The same instinct — designing learning systems that outlast direct involvement — has continued to shape my work across internal conferences, company-wide curriculum design, and most recently a 163-person external webinar on AI documentation tooling.

## The Strategy

I designed a full-cycle support ecosystem that treated technical speaking as a craft rather than an afterthought:

* **The "Science of Speaking" Curriculum:** Designed and led a multi-city training series across Austin, Seattle, and San Francisco. I translated academic rhetoric and instructional design into a 4-session technical workshop that doubled its enrollment goals.
* **End-to-End Speaker Pipeline:** Built a "Conference Quick Start Hub" that formalized the journey from the initial Call for Proposals (CFP) to compliance review and final rehearsal.
* **Executive & High-Stakes Coaching:** Provided bespoke, 1-on-1 coaching for VPs and Senior Architects, focusing on narrative flow, data visualization clarity, and public speaking anxiety.
* **Scalable Infrastructure:** Created self-directed course notes, quizzes, and documentation to ensure the program could sustain itself beyond my direct involvement.

## Internal Conference and Event Design

The same design principles applied to external speaker prep transferred directly to internal event production:

* **Platformization Unconference (2022):** Co-designed and MC'd a three-day virtual Tech Leads Unconference using open space technology — a self-organizing format where attendees propose and lead their own sessions. Built all event infrastructure: registration, communications, topic selection, and scheduling systems. MC'd the keynote AMA with the CTO. 82 authenticated attendees; 72% rated the experience as valuable (4 or 5 of 5).
* **Internal Security Conference:** Provided presentation support for the company's internal security conference, applying the same end-to-end coaching model developed for external events.
* **Internal Tech Talks:** Extended speaker support to the company's recurring public tech talk series — slide design, content development, compliance review, and rehearsal facilitation for individual presenters each quarter.

## Learning Design and Curriculum Architecture

The speaker program was always a learning design problem, not just a coaching one. I applied that lens more explicitly over time:

* **Indeed University (2020–2021):** Led curriculum architecture for the company-wide learning initiative. Conducted a full audit — 805 updates across 180 pages — and created a Curriculum Tracker that drove the Docs and Comms working group's review process. Designed the system to run without my direct involvement the following year.
* **Data University (2021):** Designed a full curriculum, certification framework, and champion enablement program for a company-wide data literacy initiative — including competency-based learning objectives, measurable exit standards, and facilitator guides — before the initiative was discontinued.
* **Workshop facilitation:** Designed and delivered workshops on writing learning objectives for team members. Organized cross-timezone participant presentation review sessions for Indeed University across U.S. and Japan.
* **"From Writer to Tool Builder" (2025):** Created and delivered a 60-minute external webinar hosted by Document360 for 163 registered technical writers on building documentation automation with AI coding agents. Designed as an enablement system — not a demo — with a hands-on GitHub repository, reusable prompt templates, team adoption frameworks, and a getting-started guide for independent implementation.

## The Impact

The program didn't just increase the volume of talks; it increased the **confidence** of the workforce.

| Metric | Outcome |
| :--- | :--- |
| **Speaker Throughput** | Supported **13–14 external talks per quarter** across global stages. |
| **Training Reach** | **70 participants** enrolled in the Science of Speaking series (200% of goal). |
| **Acceptance Rate** | **100% success rate** on assisted conference proposals in late 2019. |
| **Confidence** | **66% of participants** reported a measurable increase in public speaking confidence. |
| **Mindfulness Training** | Delivered voluntary 75-min public speaking anxiety session; **18 of 27 registrants** attended. |
| **Unconference Attendance** | **82 authenticated attendees**; 72% rated experience valuable (4 or 5 of 5). |
| **CTO AMA** | **49 attendees** at keynote session MC'd at Platformization Unconference. |
| **Curriculum Reach** | **805 updates across 180 pages** for Indeed University curriculum audit. |
| **External Webinar** | **163 registered technical writers** for "From Writer to Tool Builder" (Document360, 2025). |
